accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the central role assigned to Information and Communication Technology under the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012?
o: A mechanism limited to expanding urban telecommunications
A replacement for conventional banking institutions
A driver of growth, employment, governance reform and inclusion
An instrument exclusively for defence production
accepted.x: The policy treats ICT as a driver of economic growth, job creation, governance reform and social inclusion.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that captures the complete scope of the policy rather than a narrow sectoral role.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

accepted.s:
The twin goals of the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 included which of the following?
1. Bringing the full power of ICT within reach of the whole of India
2. Making India a Global Hub and Destination for IT and ITES Services by 2020
3. Restricting IT services to six major metropolitan hubs
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The twin goals were universal access to the benefits of ICT and making India a global hub and destination for IT and ITES services by 2020. Restricting IT to six metropolitan hubs was not a goal.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the policy’s inclusion and decentralisation objectives.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

accepted.s: In 2011–12, the Indian IT industry was valued at approximately:
accepted.x: The Indian IT industry was valued at approximately US$100 billion in 2011–12.
accepted.tq: Separate the baseline figure from the later target figures.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian IT industry in 2011–12:
1. Approximately 80% of its revenue came from exports.
2. Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune and the NCR together accounted for nearly 90% of the industry.
3. These six hubs were considered to be near saturation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The concentration and near-saturation of the six hubs encouraged the policy to promote IT in Tier II and Tier III cities.
accepted.tq: Use the complete cluster of baseline statistics and identify the option containing all correct statements.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

accepted.s: The policy emphasis on Tier II and Tier III cities was primarily intended to:
o: Shift all IT institutions away from metropolitan areas
Reduce the export orientation of the IT industry
Expand IT activity beyond saturated major hubs
Restrict ITES services to state capitals
accepted.x: The policy sought to spread IT activity to Tier II and Tier III cities because the major established hubs were highly concentrated and nearing saturation.
accepted.tq: Link the policy measure to the problem it was designed to address.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT specifically included among the areas in which the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 sought to use ICT?
o: Exclusive expansion of luxury retail markets
accepted.x: The policy specifically identified education, health, skills, financial inclusion, governance and e-literacy. Exclusive expansion of luxury retail markets was not an objective.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated option among the policy’s stated application areas.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

accepted.s:
Which of the following initiatives are described as putting the vision of the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 into practice?
1. Digital India
2. Aadhaar
3. UPI
4. BharatNet
5. DigiLocker
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Digital India, Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet and DigiLocker are all identified as initiatives that put the policy vision into practice.
accepted.tq: Check whether the comprehensive option correctly covers the full named list.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Information Technology 2012 - vision, key objectives

accepted.s: The target for IT-ITES revenue under the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 was to increase it from US$100 billion in 2012 to:
accepted.x: The policy target was to raise IT-ITES revenue from US$100 billion in 2012 to US$300 billion by 2020.
accepted.tq: Match the target year and target value, avoiding confusion with export and electronics figures.
accepted.sec: Policy targets → revenue, exports, skilled manpower, e-literacy

accepted.s: The target for IT exports under the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012 was:
o: An increase from US$100 billion to US$300 billion
An increase from US$190 billion to US$110 billion
An increase from US$69 billion to US$200 billion
An increase from US$69 billion to US$400 billion
accepted.x: The IT export target was to increase exports from US$69 billion to US$200 billion by 2020.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the export baseline and target from the separate IT-ITES revenue figures.
accepted.sec: Policy targets → revenue, exports, skilled manpower, e-literacy

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the targets of the National Policy on Information Technology, 2012.

List-I (Target)
a. IT-ITES revenue
b. IT exports
c. Skilled manpower
d. E-literacy

List-II (Target by 2020)
i. At least one e-literate person in every household
ii. US$200 billion
iii. 10 million additional skilled ICT workers
iv. US$300 billion

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: IT-ITES revenue was targeted at US$300 billion; IT exports at US$200 billion; skilled manpower at 10 million additional workers; and e-literacy at one e-literate person in every household.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure numerical pair and eliminate codes with mismatched categories.
accepted.sec: Policy targets → revenue, exports, skilled manpower, e-literacy

accepted.s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Information Technology Act
B. National Informatics Centre
C. National e-Governance Plan
D. National Task Force on IT and Software Development
accepted.x: The milestones occurred in the order NIC in 1976, National Task Force in 1998, IT Act in 2000 and NeGP in 2006.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 1998 and 2000 milestones between them.
accepted.sec: Earlier IT milestones (IT Task Force, IT Act 2000, NeGP)

accepted.s: C-DAC was set up at Pune in 1988 primarily to build the:
accepted.x: C-DAC was established at Pune in 1988 to build the PARAM supercomputer.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive technology outcome.
accepted.sec: Earlier IT milestones (IT Task Force, IT Act 2000, NeGP)

accepted.s: The National Task Force on IT and Software Development was constituted in:
accepted.x: The National Task Force on IT and Software Development dates to 1998.
accepted.tq: Use the milestone-year association rather than confusing it with the IT Act or NeGP years.
accepted.sec: Earlier IT milestones (IT Task Force, IT Act 2000, NeGP)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Information Technology Act, 2000 is correct?
1. It provided a legal basis for electronic records and digital signatures.
2. It was amended in 2008.
3. The 2008 amendment dealt, among other matters, with e-signatures and cybercrime.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The IT Act, 2000 gave legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures, and its 2008 amendment addressed e-signatures and cybercrime-related provisions.
accepted.tq: Verify the legal function, amendment year and amendment subject together.
accepted.sec: Earlier IT milestones (IT Task Force, IT Act 2000, NeGP)

accepted.s: The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP), introduced in 2006, was associated with:
o: The establishment of the first commercial semiconductor fab
The replacement of all state governments by digital bodies
accepted.x: NeGP was introduced in 2006 with Mission Mode Projects. It was not a semiconductor manufacturing programme.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct programme association and reject a neighbouring technology-sector association.
accepted.sec: Earlier IT milestones (IT Task Force, IT Act 2000, NeGP)

accepted.s: How many Mission Mode Projects are currently stated to operate under e-Kranti?
accepted.x: The stated number of Mission Mode Projects operating under e-Kranti is 44.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact programme count and distinguish it from policy targets measured in billions or millions.
accepted.sec: Earlier IT milestones (IT Task Force, IT Act 2000, NeGP)

accepted.s: The National Policy on Electronics, 2019 was approved by the Union Cabinet on:
accepted.x: The National Policy on Electronics, 2019 was approved by the Union Cabinet on 20 February 2019.
accepted.tq: Separate the policy approval date from the later dates associated with current schemes and semiconductor policy.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: The National Policy on Electronics, 2019 was approved by which ministry and replaced which earlier policy?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology; NPE 2012
accepted.x: NPE 2019 was approved by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and replaced NPE 2012.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-and-predecessor pair to distinguish closely related IT and electronics policies.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: The principal aim of the National Policy on Electronics, 2019 was to make India a global hub for:
o: Only software exports without hardware production
accepted.x: NPE 2019 aimed to establish India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing, including chipsets.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise official scope rather than a software-only interpretation.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s:
Consider the following targets of the National Policy on Electronics, 2019 to be achieved by 2025:
1. Electronics manufacturing valued at US$400 billion
2. Production of 1 billion mobile handsets annually
3. Export of 600 million mobile handsets annually
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NPE 2019 targeted US$400 billion in electronics manufacturing, 1 billion mobile handsets annually and exports of 600 million handsets annually by 2025.
accepted.tq: Check all quantitative targets together, especially the production-versus-export distinction.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the mobile manufacturing targets under NPE 2019?
o: Mobile manufacturing value of US$190 billion and mobile exports of US$110 billion
Mobile manufacturing value of US$110 billion and mobile exports of US$190 billion
Mobile manufacturing value of US$200 billion and mobile exports of US$69 billion
Mobile manufacturing value of US$400 billion and mobile exports of US$600 billion
accepted.x: The policy targeted mobile manufacturing value of US$190 billion and mobile exports of US$110 billion.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the manufacturing-value and export-value columns.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Scheme — Description
1. PLI — Large-scale electronics manufacturing
2. SPECS — Promotion of manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors
3. EMC 2.0 — Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters
4. MPMS — National e-Governance Plan Mission Mode Projects
accepted.x: MPMS is the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme; it is not a scheme for NeGP Mission Mode Projects. The first three pairs are correctly matched with NPE-related schemes.
accepted.tq: Find the single swapped programme description in a list of familiar schemes.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) is stated to cover which period?
accepted.x: MPMS is stated to cover the financial years 2026–27 to 2030–31.
accepted.tq: Read the financial-year range precisely rather than treating it as a calendar-year period.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS)?
o: It replaces SPECS and targets US$400 billion in electronics manufacturing by 2025.
It has an outlay of ₹62,500 crore, replaces PLI for large-scale electronics and targets ₹39 lakh crore production and ₹15 lakh crore exports.
It is a NeGP scheme for implementing 44 Mission Mode Projects.
It has an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore and supports only semiconductor research.
accepted.x: MPMS has a stated outlay of ₹62,500 crore, replaces PLI for large-scale electronics and targets ₹39 lakh crore production and ₹15 lakh crore exports.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its outlay, predecessor and two outcome targets.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: Electronics production in India is stated to have reached what value in 2025–26?
accepted.x: Electronics production reached ₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025–26, described as sevenfold growth under PLI.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the achieved production figure from future scheme targets and policy estimates.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: Electronics is stated to be India’s:
accepted.x: Electronics is stated to be India’s third-largest export item.
accepted.tq: Recall the ranking exactly and avoid upgrading a sector’s position to first or second.
accepted.sec: National Policy on Electronics 2019 - targets, schemes

accepted.s: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) was launched in December 2021 under the:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
accepted.x: ISM was launched in December 2021 under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
accepted.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to identify the responsible ministry.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the pillars of Semicon 2.0 and their support.

List-I (Pillar)
a. CMOS silicon fabs
b. Compound and display fabs
c. Advanced packaging
d. R&D

List-II (Maximum support)
i. 75% of project cost
ii. 35% capital subsidy
iii. 40% capital subsidy

accepted.x: The talent pillar proposes 1,00,000 additional engineers and technicians.

accepted.s: Besides Fabs, Packaging and R&D, which of the following are the other two pillars of Semicon 2.0?
accepted.x: Design and Machines/Materials are the other two pillars in addition to Fabs, Packaging and R&D.
accepted.tq: Identify the remaining members of a classified list after excluding the familiar pillars.

First commercial fab at Dholera, Gujarat

accepted.s: The Chips to Start-up (C2S) programme, launched in 2022, primarily seeks to:
o: Train 85,000 B.Tech, M.Tech and PhD students in chip design over five years
Construct 85,000 mobile towers in five years
Build 44 Mission Mode Projects under e-Kranti
accepted.x: C2S aims to develop chip-design talent by training 85,000 B.Tech, M.Tech and PhD students over five years.
accepted.tq: Match the programme’s name with its precise talent-development objective.
accepted.sec: India Semiconductor Mission - fab and ATMP units → location + company

accepted.s: Which institution implements the Chips to Start-up (C2S) programme?
accepted.x: C2S is implemented by C-DAC.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding IT institutions and their roles.

List-I (Institution)
a. MeitY
b. NASSCOM
c. STPI
d. NIC

List-II (Role)
i. Government IT/e-governance network and services
ii. Industry association of IT-BPM firms and partner in IoT CoEs
iii. Policy on IT, electronics, internet and cyber security; coordinates Digital India
iv. Export-oriented IT parks under MeitY and CoEs

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: MeitY handles policy and Digital India coordination; NASSCOM represents IT-BPM firms and partners in IoT CoEs; STPI runs export-oriented parks and CoEs; NIC provides government IT and e-governance services.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive NIC network role and eliminate codes with swapped institutional functions.
accepted.sec: IT institutions → role

accepted.s: Which of the following is a stated role of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)?
o: Licensing all Internet Service Providers exclusively
Formulating policy on IT, electronics, internet except ISP licensing, and cyber security
accepted.x: MeitY handles policy on IT, electronics, the internet other than ISP licensing, and cyber security, and coordinates Digital India.
accepted.tq: Watch the explicit exception concerning ISP licensing while identifying the ministry’s policy role.
accepted.sec: IT institutions → role

accepted.s: Which institution is described as the industry association of IT-BPM firms and a partner in IoT Centres of Excellence?
accepted.x: NASSCOM is the industry association of IT-BPM firms and is a partner in IoT Centres of Excellence.
accepted.tq: Match the industry-association function with the correct institutional acronym.
accepted.sec: IT institutions → role

accepted.s: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is associated with:
o: Training exclusively for semiconductor PhD scholars
Export-oriented IT parks under MeitY and Centres of Excellence
Legal recognition of electronic records and signatures
Government e-governance networks and services only
accepted.x: STPI operates export-oriented IT parks under MeitY and runs Centres of Excellence.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an infrastructure and export-support role from legal, network and training functions.
accepted.sec: IT institutions → role

accepted.s: Which institution provides the Government’s IT and e-governance network and services?
accepted.x: NIC provides the Government’s IT and e-governance network and services.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational network provider rather than the policy or industry body.
accepted.sec: IT institutions → role

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about C-DAC:
1. It has an R&D role involving PARAM supercomputers.
2. It implements the Chips to Start-up programme.
3. It has a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: C-DAC’s stated roles include R&D involving PARAM supercomputers, implementation of C2S and a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.
accepted.tq: Combine the institution’s historical R&D role with its current programme and location associations.
accepted.sec: IT institutions → role

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with NIELIT?
o: Government e-governance network; national IT services
Industry association of IT-BPM firms; IoT CoEs
Deemed-to-be University under MeitY; IT and electronics training
Export-oriented IT parks; software export promotion
accepted.x: NIELIT is described as a deemed-to-be University under MeitY and is associated with IT and electronics training.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional status and training role together to distinguish NIELIT from allied bodies.
accepted.sec: IT institutions → role
